label: <DEL> delimiter step in long sequences (L >= 6)
explanation: Mostly a delimiter-step unit. 84.5% of activation mass falls on the <DEL> step (t == L), where it fires 51% of the time (10x lift). How often it fires there grows with sequence length: precision at the delimiter is about 0.2-0.28 for L = 3-5, 0.40 at L=6, 0.62 at L=7 and 0.76-0.78 at L=8-9. The strongest activations (top examples near max) are all <DEL> steps in L = 8-9 sequences. A weak, scattered remainder (about 15% of mass) sits on late original-phase tokens just before <DEL> (often h, 2, g) and on early copy-phase steps, especially the first output. It is almost silent at t=0 and on mid-sequence original tokens. Which delimiters fire within a given L was not explained by first token, last token or digit count (refinements did not help). Phase==1 alone gives mass recall 0.85 at precision 0.51.
